record.paper_title: Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition)
record.original_question: In general, the radial behaviour of the derivative of a bounded analytic function in D can be pretty arbitrary; in fact, even under much stronger restrictions than just bounded, it can still be quite arbitrary. Is it true that, given any measurable function m(θ) on [0, 2π), there exists a function f (z), continuous on D and univalent on D, such that lim f ′ (reiθ ) = m(θ) r→1 for almost all θ? (In terms of known results, the conjecture seems quite plausible. Or- tel and Schneider [618] showed that the conjecture is true under slightly strengthened hypotheses; and Lohwater, Piranian and Rudin [529] showed that the conjecture is true with a slightly weakened conclusion.) (W. J. Schneider)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disc and $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ its closure. A function $f:\mathbb{D}\to\mathbb{C}$ is called univalent if it is holomorphic and injective on $\mathbb{D}$.

Prove or disprove the following statement: For every Lebesgue measurable function $m:[0,2\pi)\to\mathbb{C}$, there exists a function $f:\overline{\mathbb{D}}\to\mathbb{C}$ that is continuous on $\overline{\mathbb{D}}$ and univalent on $\mathbb{D}$ such that
$$\lim_{r\to 1^{-}} f'(re^{i\theta}) = m(\theta) \qquad \text{for almost every } \theta\in[0,2\pi).$$
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this conjecture on prescribed almost-everywhere radial limits of the derivative of a continuous univalent function on the closed unit disc. Partial results in the direction of the conjecture (under stronger hypotheses, by Ortel–Schneider, and with weakened conclusion, by Lohwater–Piranian–Rudin) are known, but no proof or disproof of the full statement was located.

status_evidence.title: On the derivative of a univalent function (Lohwater & Piranian)
status_evidence.snippet: Classical work on the radial behaviour of the derivative of univalent functions in the unit disc, providing partial results related to prescribing boundary radial limits.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for the conjecture, but no full resolution found in search.
